title: LTS channel coordinator: staged rollout gates and autoscaler handoff for GPU pools
creator: Amara Singh
description:
Goal: Implement a coordinator service and operator changes that enable safe, capacity-aware upgrades of Dedicated GPU pools across LTS channels with explicit rollout gates and autoscaler handoff semantics. This ticket covers the control-plane coordinator, drain protocol extensions, autoscaler contract changes, and the rollout gate definitions used by the Console and CLI. Scope intentionally excludes model kernel-level compatibility checks (follow-up).

Problem statement: Current upgrades either (a) rely on broad pool drains that create capacity pressure during peak workloads, or (b) perform naive canaries that don't consider autoscaler state. We need a deterministic, observable, reversible process that: (1) uses LTS channel metadata to decide compatible host images and runtime kernels, (2) coordinates draining with the autoscaler so capacity is preserved, and (3) exposes rollout gates (health checks, latency amplification, error budget consumption) that can pause/abort the upgrade and trigger fallback against a compatible fallback model variant.

Design constraints: Must be compatible with Dedicated pool semantics (reserved capacity + burst), integrate with existing node-evacuation paths, and avoid changes that require per-customer agent upgrades for initial rollout. Prefer control-plane-first approach with optional agent sidecar for finer telemetry later.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator service exists and can create a staged rollout plan for a given pool and target LTS channel (API + CLI).
Drain protocol extended: drain window negotiated with autoscaler and drain operations annotated with rollout IDs and drain-phase.
Autoscaler contract extended to accept 'hold' and 'handoff' signals from coordinator; coordinator can request temporary scaled-up burst capacity where available.
Rollout gates implemented: health gate (P95 latency + error rate), KV-cache hit regression gate, and node-level GPU utilization gate. Gates are configurable per-customer.
Console shows rollout progress per-pool with gate statuses, and operators can pause/resume/abort with one-button actions.
End-to-end test exists in CI that simulates traffic, prevents capacity loss during drain, and validates automatic rollback on gate failure.
rollout_steps: Stage 0: Dry-run plan generation (no changes) — validate plan against capacity model and LTS compatibility table.
Stage 1: Canary subset (1-2 nodes) — coordinator marks nodes and signals autoscaler to provision burst if allowed; monitor gates for 30m.
Stage 2: Progressive waves — apply drain+upgrade to waves sized by capacity headroom, with autoscaler handoff between waves.
Stage 3: Verification window — run regression prompts and live traffic checks, then mark channel as complete for pool.
Stage 4: Cleanup — release temporary burst capacity, annotate pool and export audit logs, surface post-upgrade metrics.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Autoscaler denies burst request causing capacity shortfall. Mitigation: coordinator can fallback to lower concurrency rollout or abort and notify SRE + customer-facing route to degrade non-critical workloads.

Risk: Gate signal noise causes false-positive abort. Mitigation: use rolling percentile smoothing, require 2 consecutive gate violations before abort, and allow manual override with justification recorded.
Risk: Incompatible LTS image causes silent perf regression. Mitigation: integrate quick smoke-run harness on canary nodes and require KV-cache warming checks before broad wave.
implementation_notes: Coordinator will be a lightweight control-plane service (Go) that stores plans in our existing rollout DB; new table: rollout_plans (id, pool_id, target_channel, waves, status).
Drain protocol: add rollout_id and phase field to node-drain API so that existing node agent can surface progress; no mandatory agent upgrade for 1st phase (agent will ignore unknown headers).
Autoscaler changes: extend scale API to accept 'burst_request' with expected additional gpus and duration; autoscaler evaluates budget and returns approved/delayed/denied with reason codes.
Gate metrics: use existing Console metrics (latency, error-rate) + a new KV-cache-hit metric exported from runtime. We'll add a gate-evaluator sidecar in control plane to compute gate state.
monitoring_playbook: Primary dashboard: 'Rollout Coordinator — pool <id>' showing gate statuses, wave progress, temp capacity used, and node drain progress.
Alert: rollout-gate-failure (severity P1) — triggers on abort conditions and pages platform-release oncall.
Alert: burst-capacity-denied — notifies SRE and posts to #release-ops for manual intervention.
testing_plan: Unit tests for coordinator logic and autoscaler contract mocking.
Integration test in staging: simulate 4 pools with synthetic traffic patterns to validate no net capacity loss and successful rollback on gate violation.
Chaos test: randomly delay autoscaler approval and inject node failure during wave to validate coordinator retries and pause behavior.
dependencies_notes: Relies on ENG-13011 for node evacuation ordering guarantees (must be merged before Stage 2).
RELIES ON ENG-17488 for canary fallback policies to ensure we have a fallback model variant to switch to on gate failure.
